History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
48-year-old man with 3-day history of profuse diarrhoea, central lower abdominal pain, and one episode of vomiting; clinical impression is acute infectious gastroenteritis with safety-net advice given.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Diarrhoea for 3 days.  
• Onset/progression: Sudden onset 3 days ago; frequency remains unchanged (needs to stay near toilet; sensation of incomplete evacuation).  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Central infra-umbilical abdominal pain, mild, improves slightly after bowel movement.  
  – One episode of vomiting this morning after eating fruit; preceding nausea.  
  – No visible blood in stool or vomitus.  
  – No chest pain, no new dyspnoea beyond baseline asthma, able to walk/talk.  
  – Reports sweating over past 4 days but denies clear fever.  
• Hydration/Nutrition: Likely under-hydrated; restricting oral intake to minimise bowel motions.  
• Exacerbating factors: Eating triggers urge to defecate.  
• Relieving factors: Passing stool/gas eases pain.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No rectal bleeding, no weight loss reported, no chest pain, no focal neurological symptoms.  
• Family concern: Father died of bowel cancer 10 years ago; patient worried about malignancy risk.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – uses inhaler as needed; no recent exacerbation.  
• No other chronic illnesses documented.

Medications:
• Inhaler for asthma (brand unspecified; dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
• States “NKDA” (No Known Drug Allergies).

Social History:
• Employed (missed work due to need for proximity to toilet).  
• Foreigner living in UK.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use: not discussed.

Family History:
• Father – bowel (colorectal) cancer, deceased ~10 years ago.  
• Other family history not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: not obtained (remote consult).  
• Abdominal: Patient reports mild central tenderness on self-palpation; no radiation described.  
• No other examination findings available.

Investigations:
• None performed during virtual consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected acute infectious gastroenteritis  
  • Plan:  
    – Oral rehydration: increase water/clear fluids.  
    – Dietary advice: small, light meals as tolerated.  
    – Avoid antibiotics unless bacterial infection confirmed or symptoms worsen.  
    – Monitor for red-flag symptoms: fever, bloody stool, persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, signs of dehydration.  
    – Remain at home/off work until symptoms improve (infection control).  
    – Reassessment: If no improvement or clinical deterioration within 24–48 h, arrange face-to-face GP review for physical exam, possible stool cultures, bloods, and abdominal assessment.

Issue 2: Under-hydration risk secondary to diarrhoea/vomiting  
  • Plan: Emphasise fluid intake; consider oral rehydration salts if diarrhoea continues.

Issue 3: Patient anxiety regarding family history of bowel cancer  
  • Plan: Reassured that current presentation most consistent with infection; advised future discussion with GP about appropriate colorectal cancer screening given family history.

General plan items:  
• Provide written safety-netting advice and contact details for urgent care if red-flag symptoms occur.  
• No new prescriptions issued.

Quality checks:

• Missing/expected elements: Objective vitals, formal abdominal examination, medication list reconciliation, smoking/alcohol history.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; occasional repetitions and minor inaudible phrases but core clinical content preserved.
